podcast.title: Philadelphia Origin (1983)
podcast.body: The Dead Milkmen formed in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, around 1983, at roughly the same time Camper Van Beethoven was starting. "They were formed in Philadelphia around the same time as Camp Riven Beethoven was starting in Pennsylvania in 1983."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Longevity and Reunions
podcast.body: The group remained active until 1995, briefly reformed in 2004, and has been continuously back together since 2008, maintaining their blend of punk rock and laugh-out-loud satire. "The group lasted until 1995, reformed briefly in 2004, and have been back together since 2008."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: DIY Indie Beginnings
podcast.body: The band developed as a strictly do-it-yourself project and an indie act, initially self-releasing a series of cassettes before putting out their debut album. "Like Camp R, they evolved as a strictly do-it-yourself project and as an indie act. They started by self-releasing a bunch of cassettes before they released a debut album entitled Big Lizard in My Backyard, and more albums followed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: MTV and Radio Success
podcast.body: The Dead Milkmen's videos received attention from MTV, while college radio stations embraced their music. Even a few commercial alternative radio stations of the era supported their material. "MTV jumped on some of their videos. Campers radio stations loved their stuff, and even a few commercial alternative radio stations that existed back then gave the Dead Milkman some love."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Satirical Hardcore Punk
podcast.body: While some classified them as a comedy act, The Dead Milkmen were more accurately described as satirical. They were rooted in the local hardcore scene but distinguished themselves by incorporating a sense of humor, offering a refreshing contrast to the often serious and dour American hardcore style. "The Dead Milkman were far more punk-leaning. They were part of the local hardcore scene, but differentiated themselves by showing a sense of humor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
